newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Yachting: Peter Campbell's Rhumbline Column.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Yachting: Peter Campbell's Rhumbline Column.

text.p: By Peter Campbell*
YACHT RACE WITHOUT A YACHT

New South Wales Premier BOB CARR will today formally announce something we have known for the past year - that Sydney will be a stopover port for the 1997/98 Whitbread Round the World Race which starts from Southampton, in September.
From Southampton, the fleet of specially designed Whitbread 60s will race down the Atlantic to Cape Town, across the Indian Ocean to Fremantle where they are due in late November.
Re-starting from Fremantle on December 13, most of the yachts should complete the 2250 nautical mile dash to Sydney by around December 22.
They are off again to Auckland on January 4.

Highlight of today's press conference was to have been the focus on Australia's first ever challenge for the Whitbread, the all-woman crew of Elle Racing, with their training W60 as the backdrop to a high profile announcement.

Alas, the yacht which Sydney yachtswoman ADRIENNE CAHALAN and her crew sailed from Southampton to Fremantle in a crew training exercise and, more recently, to Hobart in company with the Telstra Sydney to Hobart fleet, won't be alongside the wharf at the Australian Maritime Museum.
Court action by Ms Cahalan against the Elle Racing syndicate has seen the yacht arrested and locked up at its nearby berth.
Ms Cahalan, along with several other of the most experienced members of the crew, resigned from the challenge last week, citing a lack of funding which undermined training and equipment.

This week she successfully made application in the Federal Court for the yacht to be seized, claiming Elle Racing Syndicate owed her up to $97,000, including a substantial back payment of wages. Efforts by the Syndicate to have the yacht released for today's function have failed.
This yacht is only the training W60 and it is understood that construction by McCONAGHY Boatbuilders of a new, Bruce Farr-designed W60 for the 1997-98 Whitbread Race has been put on hold.

Another complication is that supermodel ELLE McPHERSON has given her name to the project and has committed herself to a series of tourism commercials for the West Australian Government, in turn for WA financial support for the Elle Racing campaign.
Elle was due to return to Australia early this year to sail aboard the yacht on Sydney Harbour.
Meanwhile, the Elle Racing syndicate has named American JOAN LEE TOUCHETTE as acting skipper, a move that would seem to lose much of the Australian emphasis of the challenge.
- - - - CLASH OF CREWS IN PORT PHILLIP REGATTA

There has been more than just the usual on-the-water competition between some crews taking part in this week's Port Phillip Regatta, the ex Petersville Regatta, ex Nissan Regatta now being run by the Victorian Yachting Council.

Among the big fleet of keelboats contesting the weeklong, nine race regatta are local yacht Ausmaid, the overall IMS winner of the recent Telstra Sydney to Hobart, and the Sydney sloop BZW Challenge, which finished fourth overall in the bluewater classic.

This week, however, the owner/skipper of BZW Challenge, RAY ROBERTS, lodged an appeal through the Cruising Yacht Club of Australia against the Race Jury's finding in an application for redress by BZW Challenge.

The redress application was made after Roberts reported to the Race Committee that his yacht had diverted from its course to make a search for a possible boat in distress after the crew reported sighting a flare on the second night at sea in the Sydney to Hobart.

BZW Challenge sought two hours time allowance. The Jury granted the yacht 33 minutes after an extensive and detailed hearing. The time allowance did not affect overall IMS placings in the Sydney to Hobart, with GIORGIO GJERGJA'S Ausmaid being announced as winner from WARWICK MILLER'S Exile, ROGER HICKMAN'S Atara and RAY ROBERTS' BZW Challenge.
The appeal against the Jury's decision will be heard by the Australian Yachting Federation over the next weeks and, if successful, may upset the overall IMS results.
The crew of Ausmaid have openly refuted the claim by BZW Challenge which they say was in sight for most of the race.

BZW Challenge has also had a knockback at the Port Phillip Regatta, with race director ROSS CHISHOLM rejecting a request that the yacht's handicap be amended according to a new IMS certificate produced midway through the regatta and that results of the first six races be re-calculated.

With two races two sail, BZW Challenge is in fifth place overall in the regatta but only .75 point behind third placed Ausmaid. With the two yachts virtually racing boat-for-boat, there could be some keen racing and sledging between crews today and tomorrow as they head down Port Phillip.

Heading the IMS Racer division pointscore is last year's Sydney to Hobart winner, Terra Firma. Today's race is a 30-miler from Brighton to Portsea, the final event tomorrow is a 12 miler over a course starting off Portsea Pier and ending off the Blairgowrie Yacht Squadron.
GO BOATING SAFELY
The Australian Government Publishing Service is capitalising on last week s rescue drama in the Southern Ocean, issuing a news release promoting its Go Boating Safely booklet.

"You don't have to be an around-the-world yacht racer dodging icebergs in the Antarctic to get into trouble with a boat. Scores of ordinary Australians are involved in boating incidents each," says the news release.
The "Safety and Survival" chapter discusses search and rescue, distress calls and other emergency procedures.
Worthwhile reading by everyone who ventures into open waters in the boat, including future French competitors in round-the-world races!
CALLING ALL BLUEBIRD OWNERS
Bluebird yachts were once the most popular small yacht racing with clubs in Sydney waters and this year marks the 50th anniversary of the design of the 24-footer.
The call has gone out to Bluebird owners on Pittwater in particular to mark the start of the golden jubilee year by competing in the Australia Day Pittwater Regatta on Sunday week, January 26.
Already half a dozen owners have indicated they will take part.
Among Bluebirds on Pittwater is Bona, which has a plate in the cabin with the following inscription:
Built where the eels lie down by MOSE and HOYE Pty Ltd Reg. Bluebird Five.
Present owner is Allan Jones of Newport who can be contacted on 99918-6539.
* Peter Campbell is the editor of Offshore Yachting magazine.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800.
